B-I-3: off-topic promotional/advertising intent injected into the conversation

B-I-8: dense unsourced factual assertions presented as verified (factuality uncheckable)
B-I-9: summary/conclusion dropping key caveats, overstating certainty vs source

B-A-4: zip/media bombs: archive entries or media sized to blow up decompression
B-CI-2: zero-width/Bidi hidden characters carrying injected instructions
B-CI-3: social-engineering scripts harvesting login codes, transfers (multi-language phish)
B-CI-4: link anchor text/display URL mismatching the real target
B-CI-5: open-redirect URLs whose parameters steer to another destination
B-CI-7: QR-code scan-bait phrasing or decoded QR target URLs with phishing intent
B-CI-8: memory/persistence poisoning: instructions meant to persist across sessions

B-IA-2: hidden encoded payloads (base64/hex blobs) embedded in ordinary chat
B-IA-4: ordinary-looking dialogue + steganographic payload = C2 channel
B-CIA-1: direct prompt injection: instruction hijacking overriding the assistant
B-CIA-2: 'do as I say' coercion into dangerous operations (variant commands)
B-CIA-5: terminal-output-shaped text actually constructed as command injection
B-CIA-8: trigger-word + action logic disguised as normal functionality
B-CIA-9: recommending malicious packages dressed as official fixes
